_comment: ClawFactory egress policy. Root-owned, /etc/clawfactory/egress-policy.json, root:root 0644.
TWO SECTIONS. BOTH ARE ENFORCED, BY DIFFERENT MECHANISMS.
read_fetch   -- destinations the agent may fetch from. Guard 3 enforces this section.
send_actions -- approval-gated destinations. Guard 2 enforces this section.
HOW read_fetch IS ENFORCED. clawfactory-read-fetch.sh resolves each listed host and
rebuilds the nft set @read_fetch_ipv4, which the egress chain accepts on tcp dport 443.
That is FIREWALL-ENFORCED, and it therefore holds against the agent's shell as well as
against its fetch tool, because the chain filters by uid rather than by process.
read_fetch IS EMPTY BY DEFAULT AND THAT IS THE FAIL-CLOSED STATE. Guard 3 does not
create the denial: the chain already ends in a terminal drop for uid 1000, so an
unlisted destination was unreachable before Guard 3 existed. What Guard 3 adds is the
user's ability to open and close a named hole, from Studio, through a root-only tool.
WHAT read_fetch DOES NOT CLAIM. Matching is by resolved ADDRESS, because that is what
an nftables set holds. A host that shares an address with something already reachable
is reachable whether or not it is listed here, and the provider route is always
reachable. Guard 3's claim is about destinations the user has NOT approved being
denied; it is not a claim that only the listed hostnames are reachable.
toolchain IS THE USER'S SWITCH OVER THE SOFTWARE-SOURCE ROUTE, and it DEFAULTS ON.
clawfactory-toolchain.sh enforces it through the nft set @toolchain_ipv4, which it
flushes and rebuilds on every run, including the five-hourly refresh. The hosts it
covers are the skill hub, GitHub and npm; the list itself is a root-owned constant in
that script, not a value anyone edits here.
WHY ON RATHER THAN OFF. Off would ship a product where npm and GitHub fail on a fresh
box, which is a functional regression rather than a safety win. It buys no honesty
either: the product's claim sentence names the software sources explicitly. The switch
only ever NARROWS what is reachable, so the claim holds in both positions. An ABSENT
toolchain key means a policy file written before this feature and is read as ON; an
unreadable file denies, because a fault is not a preference.
WHAT OFF DOES NOT DO. It does NOT stop skill installation, and this paragraph used to
say that it did. Measured on cfv-169: a real `openclaw skills install` completed with
the switch off, because clawhub.ai resolves to an address it shares with openclaw.ai,
a permanent base host no toggle can revoke. That is the address-scoping residual above,
applied to this switch, and it must be stated wherever the switch is described.
THE PROVIDER ROUTE IS NOT AFFECTED BY THIS SWITCH and must never be. It lives in
@allowed_ipv4, and an agent that cannot reach its model is a bricked product.
send_actions IS EMPTY BY DEFAULT AND THAT IS THE FAIL-CLOSED STATE. No destination is
permitted until the user configures SMTP in Studio, which is the act that authorizes
exactly one host and port. A fresh install can enqueue nothing and send nothing.
HOW send_actions IS ENFORCED, stated precisely because the wrong description is easy to
write and hard to unwrite. The send broker reads this file and refuses any destination
not listed here. That is BROKER-ENFORCED, in root-owned code reading a root-owned file.
It is NOT firewall-enforced. The nft chain begins `meta skuid != 1000 return`, which
leaves every non-1000 uid unfiltered by construction, so the broker's ability to reach
SMTP is emergent rather than granted. There is no firewall exemption for the broker and
none should ever be added.
It remains structural with respect to the AGENT, because the agent cannot modify
root-owned code or this file. Matching is exact on host and port. No wildcards: a
wildcard in a send destination is an exfiltration channel with a friendly name.

read_fetch._note: Enforced by Guard 3 through the nft set read_fetch_ipv4. Empty means the agent can fetch nothing beyond the provider route and, while the toolchain switch is on, the software sources. Managed from Studio; the agent has no write path.

toolchain._note: Enforced by clawfactory-toolchain.sh through the nft set toolchain_ipv4. true means the agent can reach the skill hub, GitHub and npm. false closes that route and stops the agent fetching code from GitHub and npm. It does NOT stop skill installation: the skill hub shares a network address with ClawFactory's own site, which this switch does not cover, and a real skills install was measured completing with the switch off. Never affects the AI provider. Managed from Studio; the agent has no write path.
